chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī and Abū Qatādah ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥafṣ al-Qummī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about al-Aḍḥā: how long is it in Minā? He said: Four days. And I asked him about al-Aḍḥā outside Minā, and he said: Three days. I said: What do you say about a traveling man who arrives two days after al-Aḍḥā—may he offer the sacrifice on the third day? He said: Yes.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَيَّامٍ: the number of days for sacrifice in Minā
key_terms.بِمِنًى: in Minā, the hajj location where the sacrifice period is longer
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ: the number of days for sacrifice outside Minā
key_terms.مُسَافِرٍ: a traveler whose delayed arrival affects the timing of the sacrifice

ai.seo_question: How many days may the Eid al-Aḍḥā sacrifice be performed in Minā and outside Minā?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the days in which the sacrifice of al-Aḍḥā may be performed. It distinguishes between Minā, where the period is four days, and places other than Minā, where it is three days, and it confirms that a traveler arriving late may still offer the sacrifice on the third day.
